scenes.heading: Nutrient cycles
scenes.sub: The carbon in you may once have been in a gum tree
scenes.say: The carbon in your body may once have been part of a gum tree, a dinosaur or the air. Unlike energy, the materials living things are made of get used again and again.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Pull apart a Lego car and build a house from the same bricks
scenes.science: Atoms are recycled between living things and the environment
scenes.breaks: Lego bricks stay the same, but atoms are rearranged into new molecules, like carbon in CO₂ becoming glucose.
scenes.say: Earth doesn't get new matter, just like a Lego box doesn't get new bricks. You pull a model apart and build something new. Atoms work the same way, and decomposers are the ones pulling the models apart. Energy flows, matter cycles.

scenes.heading: The carbon cycle
scenes.say: In the carbon cycle, photosynthesis takes carbon dioxide out of the air. Respiration, decomposition and combustion put it back. Burning fossil fuels releases carbon locked away for millions of years, faster than sinks can absorb it, so atmospheric carbon dioxide rises.

scenes.heading: Why nitrogen is tricky
points: Plants can't use N₂: strong triple bond
Plants absorb nitrate from the soil
scenes.say: Nitrogen is needed to make proteins and DNA. About seventy-eight percent of the air is nitrogen gas, but plants can't use it, because of its strong triple bond. Plants absorb nitrate from the soil instead. Bacteria do most of the work.
scenes.caption: Nitrogen is needed to make proteins and DNA. About 78% of the air is nitrogen gas (N₂), but plants can't use it, because of its strong triple bond. Plants absorb nitrate from the soil instead. Bacteria do most of the work.

scenes.heading: The nitrogen cycle
scenes.say: Fix it, nitrify it, absorb it, rot it, release it. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria, like Rhizobium in legume root nodules, turn nitrogen gas into ammonium. Nitrifying bacteria make nitrate. Plants absorb it. Decomposers release ammonium from dead things. And denitrifying bacteria in soggy soil send nitrogen back to the air.

scenes.heading: The water cycle
scenes.say: Water cycles through evaporation, transpiration from leaves through tiny pores called stomata, condensation into clouds, precipitation, and runoff. Clearing forests reduces transpiration, which can reduce local rainfall.

scenes.heading: Decomposition experiment
scenes.question: 20 g of leaf litter left for 8 weeks. Mass remaining: cold and dry 18 g, warm and moist 9 g, warm and dry 15 g.
lines: Warm and moist lost the most
scenes.say: Leaf litter left for eight weeks lost the most mass in warm, moist conditions: eleven grams. Decomposers' enzymes work faster in warmth, and they need water. In cold, dry or waterlogged places, dead material builds up.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Energy flows, but matter cycles. Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide, and respiration and combustion return it. Bacteria drive the nitrogen cycle, and decomposers close every loop. Now try the practice questions!
